title: Rapid customer feedback loop and status drivers — SRE comms playbook
summary: Working draft: lightweight SRE runbook focusing on incident communications that close the loop with customers (status page + targeted customer outreach) and internal war-room checklist emphasizing time-to-first-update, impact estimation, and triage ownership.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a short, practical playbook for incident communications with a focus on reducing customer uncertainty and surfacing actionable feedback to product/rv teams. The idea is to prioritize timely, honest updates and an operational feedback loop so post-incident analysis is informed by customer signal (not just metrics).

Audience:
- SRE on-call and bridge owner
- Product manager / owner of the affected service
- Support/CS leads for impacted accounts
- Comms/Legal as needed for high severity or regulated customers

Design goals (why different):
1) Fast cadence: first public update within 15 minutes for Sev1/2, 30 minutes for Sev3 if customer-visible.
2) Tiered messaging: use the same source-of-truth text but customize customer outreach by segment (free, paid, enterprise).
3) Feedback capture: include an embedded short feedback ask (checkbox + free text) in enterprise follow-ups to collect whether the incident caused data loss, business impact, or downstream outages.
4) Actionable artefacts: each update must include "next action" and "owner" fields so follow-ups are assigned.

Definitions/Severity & expectations:
- Sev 1 (critical): service unavailable or major functional loss for multiple customers. First public update: 15 min. Hourly updates until recovery or stable mitigation.
- Sev 2 (major): degraded latency/throughput causing user-facing errors for a segment. First public update: 15 min. Updates every 2 hours.
- Sev 3 (minor): single-customer issue or non-critical regression. First public update: 30–60 min if customer-visible.

Timeboxes and responsibilities (quick):
- T+0–5m: Pager fires, primary oncall joins (bridge) and posts short "investigating" signal on Slack #sre-incident and triage.
- T+5–15m: Bridge owner determines severity, impact estimate, and owner for customer comms. Prepare first status page message (template below).
- T+15–60m: Publish public update, notify CS for enterprise customers and open dedicated Slack threads/Zoom for top customers.
- T+60m+: Repeat updates per severity cadence, track actions in JIRA ticket, escalate to PM/Eng director if not progressing.

Status page templates (concise; use minimum friction):
- Initial (published publicly)
  Title: [Incident {incident_id}] Degraded {service_name} – Investigating
  Body: We are aware of and investigating reports that {service_name} is experiencing {short-symptom}. Our engineers are actively investigating. Impact: {estimate_customers_or_percent}. Next update: {ETA or time window}. Incident owner: {owner_name}.
  Visibility: public (all), tag: {severity}.

- Update (progress)
  Title: [Incident {incident_id}] Update – {service_name} – {brief-status}
  Body: Summary of actions taken since last update (bullets), current impact (improved/worse, remaining percent or flow), next steps (what we will do next), ETA if known, contact for enterprise customers.

- Resolved
  Title: [Incident {incident_id}] Resolved – {service_name}
  Body: Root cause (short), mitigation applied, customer impact summary (duration, who affected), follow-up/next steps (postmortem schedule, link), owner.

Customer email / targeted outreach templates (short + variations):
- Enterprise proactive notification (first outreach)
  Subject: Incident {incident_id}: {service_name} degraded – we are investigating
  Body: Hi {customer_contact},
  We’re currently investigating an issue affecting {service_name}. Impact we see: {impact_description: e.g., failed API calls for some requests}. We recognize this may affect your workflows. Our engineers are working on a fix; next update by {ETA}. If this causes immediate business impact for you, please reply with "URGENT" and we’ll prioritize a dedicated update/bridge.
  Sent by: SRE oncall ({oncall_name}) and CS lead ({cs_name})

- Enterprise follow-up (after mitigation)
  Subject: Incident {incident_id} – mitigation complete and next steps
  Body: Hi {customer_contact},
  We have mitigated the issue affecting {service_name}. Summary: {one-line root cause + mitigation}. Impact window: {start_time} to {end_time}. Did this cause data loss or downstream failures? [Yes/No] (please reply). We’re scheduling a post-incident review and will follow up with a write-up and any customer-specific remediation items.

- Public shorter notice (for large customer-base)
  For general customers, use status page and a short tweet-style update: "We’re investigating {service_name} issues; follow status.redwood.ai/{incident_id} for updates." Avoid jargon, link to status page.

Internal war-room checklist (stripdown, usable as pinned paste in bridge):
- Before publishing anything: confirm severity and scope (metric + at least 2 customer reports or synthetic fail).
- Establish bridge roles (ops lead, comms lead, PM owner, SRE tracer, CS liaison, oncall backup).
- Metrics to watch: 95th/99th latency, error rate by region, queue length, GPU utilization, retry/backoff patterns.
- Immediate mitigations (do first): traffic redirect, scale up shards, fail open to a safe degraded mode, toggle feature flags.
- Communication steps: draft status page initial -> post -> notify CS -> create customer follow-ups list (spreadsheet) -> send targeted emails to top-10 impacted customers.
- Track actions in JIRA: create incident-{incident_id} with labels [committed-fix, rollback, customer-followup]. Assign owners & ETA.
- Post-resolution: schedule follow-up meeting within 72 hours and assign postmortem writer.

Customer impact estimator (quick heuristic):
- Small: < 5 customers or less than 0.5% of requests affected.
- Medium: 5–50 customers or 0.5–5% of requests.
- Large: >50 customers or >5% requests.
Use estimator to decide whether to escalate to CS lead/Exec comms.

Feedback loop and outcomes capture (unique part):
- Immediately after resolution: CS sends a 2-question survey to enterprise contacts (impact severity + business effect). Add answers as comments in the incident ticket.
- During postmortem: product/rv team reviews customer feedback and tags any follow-up code changes as customer-driven.
- Scorecard metric: Time between first public update and first customer response; target < 48h for enterprise customers.

Templates for short Slack comms (bridge to #sre-incident):
- Investigating: "[INVESTIGATING] {incident_id} {service_name} – symptoms: {short}. Bridge: {link}. Owner: {owner}."
- Update: "[UPDATE] {incident_id} - {brief} - impact: {estimate} - next: {next_step}"
- Resolved: "[RESOLVED] {incident_id} - summary: {one-line}. Postmortem on {date}."

Post-incident follow-ups (actionable closure):
- Postmortem should include root cause, timeline, impact (metric + customer list), corrective actions, and a specific owner for each action with ETA.
- CS outreach summary: add the list of customers contacted and any replies to the incident JIRA.
- Long-term detection: create an alert or synthetic that would have caught this earlier; include alert runbook if applicable.

Open questions / to iterate on:
- Should we auto-open a dedicated Zoom/phone bridge for any enterprise customer reply of "URGENT"? (current practice: manual)
- How to structure an automated feedback form for enterprise customers that plugs into JIRA without manual copying?
- Which customer segments get SMS vs email vs Slack pings? (needs GTM input)

Notes / references:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-INC-COMMS-2024 (archived templates)
- Internal Slack: #sre-incident, #cs-enterprise-alerts

Usage guidance: keep updates short, authoritative, and consistent across channels. The aim is to reduce repeated customer outreach and place friction on internal decision making: every update must move the incident forward or assign a clear owner.

Draft history: created 2025-01-09 by Taylor Chen. Iterations: 2025-01-21 (added feedback loop), 2025-02-12 (refined timeboxes).
customer_email_template:
Subject: Incident {incident_id}: {service_name} status

Hi {customer_contact},

We wanted to let you know we're investigating an issue affecting {service_name}. Impact: {brief_impact}. We're on it and will update by {eta}. If you're seeing production blockers, reply with URGENT and include your customer id: {customer_id}.

SRE oncall: {oncall_name}
CS contact: {cs_name}

Thanks for your patience,
The Redwood Inference Team
internal_warroom_checklist:
1) Confirm severity and metrics thresholds.
2) Claim bridge and assign roles.
3) Publish initial status page message (15m for Sev1/2).
4) Notify CS + compile impacted-customer spreadsheet.
5) Post short Slack notice to #sre-incident and #cs-enterprise-alerts.
6) Apply immediate mitigations and document steps in ticket.
7) Maintain updates cadence until stable.
8) After mitigation, publish resolved message and notify enterprise customers.
9) Schedule postmortem and collect customer feedback.
10) Close with action items assigned and timelines.
notes_to_self: Keep this doc short and pragmatic. Avoid long forms in public updates; link to postmortem for details. Iterate templates after two real incidents to see what phrases reduce follow-up pings.
audience_notes: Use this for oncall training. CS should customize enterprise emails with account context (SLA references, contract numbers). Legal should review any message that mentions data loss.
